title: Wely — machines & JVMs
description: The two machines of the cluster side by side, and the JVMs on them. Every node-level query is grouped by node: before 2026-10-29 they averaged both machines into one number, which was true of neither.

panels.title: What runs where
panels.description: One row per service and the machine its pod is on, from the node label the scrape config attaches to every pod series. Placement is deliberate — see the project's CLAUDE.md — so this table is the check that the cluster matches it.

panels.title: Written to disk since boot
panels.description: Cumulative bytes written to each machine's main block device, from boot. The Pi writes to an SD card — the part that fails first on these machines — which is why the datastores moved to the SSD node. This is the number that justified the move, so it is the one to watch.

panels.title: Write rate per machine
panels.description: Bytes per second written per machine. Four of the five continuous writers — Kafka, both PostgreSQL and Neo4j — left the SD card on 2026-10-29; MongoDB and Garage stayed. The Pi's line is what they still cost it.

panels.title: Inter-node traffic (tailscale0)
panels.description: Everything between the two nodes rides the tailnet: serverwely1 registered its kubelet with its Tailscale address, so flannel, the kubelet and pod-to-pod traffic all cross this interface. It is the cost of the split — and the reason a service sits on the machine that holds its data.

panels.title: CPU temperature

targets.expr: max by (node) (node_thermal_zone_temp{type=~"cpu-thermal|cpu_thermal|x86_pkg_temp", node=~"$node"}) or max by (node) (node_hwmon_temp_celsius{node=~"$node"})

panels.description: The SoC sensor on the Pi (cpu-thermal) and the package sensor on the x86 node. A Raspberry Pi 5 throttles at 85°C; the Pentium is rated far higher.

targets.expr: node_load1{node=~"$node"} / on(node) group_left() count by (node) (count by (node, cpu) (node_cpu_seconds_total{node=~"$node"}))

panels.title: Disk free per mount point
panels.description: Free space. Prometheus and every claim are local-path directories on /.

panels.title: CPU temperature

targets.expr: max by (node) (node_thermal_zone_temp{type=~"cpu-thermal|cpu_thermal|x86_pkg_temp", node=~"$node"}) or max by (node) (node_hwmon_temp_celsius{node=~"$node"})

panels.description: The SoC sensor on the Pi (cpu-thermal) and the package sensor on the x86 node. A Raspberry Pi 5 throttles at 85°C; the Pentium is rated far higher.

panels.title: CPU by mode

targets.expr: sum by (node, mode) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode!="idle", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])) / on(node) group_left() count by (node) (count by (node, cpu) (node_cpu_seconds_total{node=~"$node"}))

panels.description: Share of the four cores spent in each mode; idle left out.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Used = total minus what the kernel reports as available (page cache included).

panels.title: Network
panels.description: The node's own interfaces, from the kubelet's cAdvisor (root cgroup): node-exporter runs in the pod network and cannot see them. Outgoing below the axis.

panels.title: Memory vs limit

targets.expr: max by (node, pod, container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{job="kubelet-cadvisor", container!="", node=~"$node"}) / max by (node, pod, container) (container_spec_memory_limit_bytes{job="kubelet-cadvisor", container!="", node=~"$node"} > 0)

panels.description: Working set over memory limit, per container: the kernel OOM-kills at 100%.

panels.title: Memory working set
panels.description: Working set per container (solid) and its limit (dashed).

panels.title: Container CPU
panels.description: Cores used per container (1 = one full core).

panels.title: CPU throttling

targets.expr: sum by (node, pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{job="kubelet-cadvisor", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (node, pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{job="kubelet-cadvisor", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.description: Share of CFS periods in which the pod hit its CPU limit (reported per pod by this kubelet). Sustained throttling slows a JVM down long before it shows in CPU usage.

panels.title: Heap used vs max
panels.description: Heap used (solid) against its maximum (dashed), all pools summed.

panels.title: GC time
panels.description: Share of wall-clock time spent in GC pauses.

panels.title: Process CPU
panels.description: CPU used by the JVM, as a share of the CPUs it can see.
